review_notes: I inspected the full target file and compared its list Cartesian-product definition with Batteries’ List.product. I found one avoidable competing definition. The remaining inspected declarations did not have a sufficiently evidenced Mathlib/core/Batteries counterpart under this rubric.

findings.excerpt:
def cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) : List (α × β) :=
  xs.flatMap fun x => ys.map fun y => (x, y)
findings.problem: This independently defines the generic Cartesian product of two lists, with the same element order and implementation as Batteries’ existing List.product. The target then builds its triples and counting proofs around the separate cart name, so code using the existing API must bridge between two names for the same list operation.
findings.proposed_change: Use List.product directly for triples and the counting lemmas, or retain cart as a thin abbreviation of List.product while migrating its implementation-dependent proofs to the existing API.
findings.benefit: Consolidates the generic Cartesian-product operation with the standard list API, reducing duplicate names and avoiding repeated conversions for users or proofs that combine this code with List.product.

evidence.excerpt:
def cart (xs : List α) (ys : List β) : List (α × β) :=
  xs.flatMap fun x => ys.map fun y => (x, y)
def product (l₁ : List α) (l₂ : List β) : List (α × β) := l₁.flatMap fun a => l₂.map (Prod.mk a)
